method: After a shared NPC death the host owns the corpse: it streams the body while the client holds its ragdoll animated at the host pose (the native physics mode switch, 1113d/1117), and the ragdoll is released to native physics when the channel stops (chapter 86, corpse authority). The takedown harness with -CorpseRelease (1254o) films the kill from above (a drop assassination on tutorial guard 2, product controller) and then samples the victim in both worlds every ~170 ms through the release: the client's corpse entry goes from streamed to disabled, the body is released and must settle where the host's body lies. Each case passes when the remote takedown phase is presented, the outcome is the same in both worlds (dead) and the two corpses end within 2 m (measured: 0.02 m for Corvo's kill, 0.37 m for Emily's). A client-sourced kill (1254t+) also samples both worlds and pitches the observer camera down so the body stays in frame. The player character's own death is the authored collapse of audit 1357; dropping a carried body belongs to carry_body_lift_idle_move_drop_throw.

items.scope: NPC corpse hand-off from the takedown scene to ragdoll and to shared corpse authority, for kills by either player, with the release filmed in the observer world and the bodies ending together in both worlds.

visual.verdict: Corvo drops onto the guard; the body slumps out of the takedown into a sprawl on the floorboards and lies still, ending 2 cm from the host body.
Emily lands on the guard and drives him face down at her feet; the body then slackens and rolls into a sprawl beside her and stays down, ending 0.37 m from the same body in the joiner world.
